transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-09 16:00 UTC | Duration 75m | Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (SolarWave Head of Cloud Security), Meera Patel (SRE Lead), Tomás Rivera (Compliance)

00:00 Jordan Blake: hey everyone thanks for carving out the time, we'll run through our security posture, the SOC2 artifacts, and then walk through how we handle incidents and escalations. Priya's gonna lead the tech bits.
00:18 Liam Ortiz: great, thanks. just to set context, SolarWave is in the middle of an enterprise procurement; team cares a lot about BYOK, eu residency for eu customers, and measurable RTO numbers.
00:30 Priya Menon: sounds good. quick agenda: SOC2 status, auth (SSO/SAML + RBAC), audit logs & retention, KMS options incl BYOK/HSM, then incident + BCDR walkthrough incl runbooks and pager escalation tiers.
00:47 Meera Patel: quick Q up front — our SREs want to know how KV cache state is handled during failover, and whether prefix caching can be restored without user-impact.
00:59 Priya Menon: good callout. our runtime persists minimal KV state; we support checkpointing to object storage and have fast warm-start paths — it's often described as KV "cash" in notes, sorry, 'cache' — sometimes transcript does that — but practical impact is usually small; warm-up may add a few hundred milliseconds.
01:20 Tomás Rivera: from compliance: can you confirm SOC2 Type II coverage window and whether audit logs are tamper-evident?
01:31 Jordan Blake: we completed SOC2 Type II for a rolling 12-month period ending 2026-03. We'll share the summary and redacted report. logs are hashed and stored with immutability controls; retention configurable per customer, default 90 days.
01:45 Liam Ortiz: 90 days is tight for us; we need 365 days for certain systems in EU. Is longer retention possible and where are logs stored regionally?
01:58 Priya Menon: yes, retention is configurable up to multiple years. For EU residency we can keep logs in eu-west regions; we integrate with customer VPC for Private deployments and can also push logs to customer-controlled S3 in-region.
02:16 Meera Patel: ok KMS: we need BYOK with rotation control, HSM-backed keys, and audit trail. how are keys used — do you hold any plaintext?
02:28 Priya Menon: we never store customer plaintext. KMS is used to encrypt model artifacts and customer data at rest. BYOK is supported for Private deploys and Dedicated via KMS key-proxy; HSM is supported via our KMS partner integrations. Key rotation is customer-driven; we support zero-downtime key rotation via staged keys and rewrap processes.
02:49 Tomás Rivera: any blind spots with streaming or ephemeral tokens?
02:55 Priya Menon: streaming keeps ephemeral tokens in-memory on the runtime node; they aren't written to disk unless explicitly configured in logs; we redaction filter sensitive keys in telemetry by default.
03:10 Liam Ortiz: let's pivot to incident response and BCDR. Our requirements: RTO 15 minutes for inference control-plane, RPO 5 minutes for KV cache, and 99.95% uptime for critical inference endpoints. can Redwood meet that?
03:25 Jordan Blake: we tier SLAs. Hosted API standard SLA is 99.9; Dedicated has higher target and we can commit to 99.95 with reserved capacity and runbook alignment. RTO/RPO depends on deployment mode and config; Dedicated with multi-az pools and prefix caching warmed can meet RTO ~10–15m.
03:52 Meera Patel: what's the failover mechanism? do you use active-active across AZs or active-passive with warm standbys?
04:01 Priya Menon: we typically recommend active-active for low-latency regions — requests are routed via smart routing with health checks and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant. For on-prem or private we provide orchestrated failover scripts that SREs can trigger; we also support automated canary failovers.
04:25 Liam Ortiz: escalation process — how many tiers, who gets paged, and can we hook into our PagerDuty with custom runbooks?
04:34 Jordan Blake: three-tiered: Tier 1 on-call SRE (customer) with Redwood first responder (level: infra on-call), Tier 2 Redwood SE/Platform engineer, Tier 3 Engineering + Product. We integrate with PagerDuty and can push alerts and runbook links. Customers can attach custom playbooks; Priya will share sample runbook templates.
04:58 Meera Patel: do you keep post-incident records and a timeline export? Compliance wants the full audit trail for breach response.
05:06 Priya Menon: yes, incident timelines, runbooks, and config diffs are exportable; we persist these with linkable IDs and also store change events in the audit log. We support egress to customer storage for long-term retention.
05:25 Tomás Rivera: tabletop drill idea — we want to simulate a region outage with degraded KV cache and verify failover. how long do these exercises take?
05:34 Priya Menon: typically 2 hours: 30m intro & objectives, 60m scenario execution plus role play and runbooks, 30m lessons learned and action items. We'll run one with your ops and Redwood SEs.
05:48 Liam Ortiz: can we measure token-level reconciliation post-failover to ensure no data loss?
05:56 Priya Menon: yes, we can produce token/delta reconciliation reports comparing pre/post KV snapshots. they are part of our BCDR pack.
06:08 Meera Patel: in terms of legal hold and e-discovery, can audit logs be snapshot and sealed for litigation?
06:16 Jordan Blake: yes, we have an archival workflow to lock logs and produce chain-of-custody metadata; we can provide that as part of Private deployments or as an add-on for Hosted.
06:27 Tomás Rivera: networking — do you require specific firewall rules and can you support restrictive egress?
06:33 Priya Menon: for Private, outbound is minimal and we can operate in strict egress-only scenarios; for dedicated we need a control-plane channel for telemetry, but that's configurable to use customer endpoints.
06:48 Liam Ortiz: what about service degradations — do you throttle or serve degraded model variants to preserve availability? we prefer graceful degradation over total outage.
06:56 Priya Menon: we have automatic fallback policies — route to smaller or quantized model variants to keep responses, with a note in headers that quality may differ. That keeps the endpoint up with reduced cost/latency profile.
07:10 Meera Patel: real-world question — if a region goes down and the KMS provider is unreachable, are keys cached locally?
07:18 Priya Menon: we don't cache plaintext keys; we maintain short-lived encryption envelopes that allow limited decrypt operations during temporary key provider outages, but full key unavailability will prevent decrypt of new artifacts; that's why we recommend multi-provider KMS setups for critical services.
07:36 Liam Ortiz: okay let's capture concrete acceptance criteria: 1) RTO <= 15m for control-plane, 2) RPO <= 5m for KV cache, 3) 365d audit log retention stored EU-region for EU tenants, 4) BYOK with HSM and rotation support, 5) successful tabletop drill with no manual intervention beyond 2nd tier.
07:58 Jordan Blake: noted. Priya — can we map these to a proposed Dedicated deployment config?
08:06 Priya Menon: yes. Proposed: Dedicated multi-az GPU pool in eu-west, KMS BYOK via customer HSM, persistent audit logs pushed to customer S3 for 365d retention, autoscaling policy with reserve capacity to hit 99.95% SLA, runbook + PagerDuty integration. I'll produce a config doc.
08:26 Meera Patel: one more — encryption in transit, do you support mTLS between customer app and runtime?
08:33 Priya Menon: yes, mTLS supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports HTTPS with client cert options for enterprise customers.
08:43 Tomás Rivera: compliance question — do you re-run SOC2 when significant infra changes happen?
08:50 Jordan Blake: major infra changes trigger control reviews and we update our SOC2 disclosure; we also publish a changelog of security-relevant infra changes.
09:02 Liam Ortiz: any public pen-tests or bug-bounty results?
09:07 Priya Menon: we do annual pen tests and run a private bug-bounty program; we can share a summary of findings and mitigation timelines.
09:18 Meera Patel: cool. next steps recap?
09:22 Jordan Blake: I'll send SOC2 artifacts and the redacted report; Priya will send runbook templates, and we'll schedule the tabletop for week of 2026-06-22. Meera/Tomás to share RTO/RPO spreadsheet by 2026-06-12.
09:38 Tomás Rivera: sounds good. thanks all.
09:44 Jordan Blake: thanks everyone, bye.

End of transcript.
notes: Customer concerned about EU data residency and long retention. Priya recommended Dedicated with KMS BYOK and customer S3 for long-term logs. Agreed to tabletop drill week of 2026-06-22. Jordan to share SOC 2 artifacts and compliance pack.
